sources.news_title: San Francisco 49ers Coach Kyle Shanahan Injured in Car Crash Ahead of Training Camp
sources.text:
San Francisco 49ers coach Kyle Shanahan is on the mend after a tragic accident.
The NFL team announced that its head coach was injured in a car accident amid the league's summer break and will participate in training camp in a limited capacity during his recovery.
"San Francisco 49ers Head Coach Kyle Shanahan was involved in a car accident last week where he suffered non-life-threatening injuries," the 49ers shared in a statement on the team's social media channels July 25. "Coach Shanahan will participate in team activities on a limited basis at the start of training camp while he recovers. Coach Shanahan and the 49ers organization would like to sincerely thank all first responders involved for their efforts and care."
On July 14, Shanahan—who has been the head coach of the 49ers since 2017—crashed into an SUV near his home in northern California, suffering a concussion, breaking his nose, multiple ribs and his hand, according to multiple outlets, citing sources close to the situation. The 46-year-old also reportedly required 40 stitches in his face.
Shanahan was transported to a local hospital, before he was discharged later that day, according to Palo Alto Lt. Nicholas Martinez, per CNN.
Additionally, Martinez noted that drugs and alcohol were not a factor in the collision.
While he added that neither Shanahan nor the other driver was cited for the accident and they both cooperated with police, he didn't disclose any further details about the crash.
"Consistent with our standard release of information procedures in such cases," Martinez shared, "we do not release information regarding the cause of the collision, or which party may have been at fault."
As Shanahan recovers at home, assistant head coach Chris Foerster and other team coordinators "will handle head coach responsibilities," the 49ers noted in its statement.
The football team's upcoming season will mark Shanahan's 10th overall. During his years as head coach, he's led the Niners to two trips to the Super Bowl in 2019 and 2023.
The team announced the news of Shanahan's accident on the first day of training camp. The 49ers' first game, against the Los Angeles Rams, will take place on Sept. 10 in Melbourne, Australia.

sources.text:
San Francisco 49ers coach Kyle Shanahan suffers concussion, broken nose and fractured ribs in car crash
Shanahan suffered a concussion, a broken nose, several fractured ribs, and hand injuries in the crash
San Francisco 49ers head coach Kyle Shanahan has sustained multiple injuries in a car crash earlier this month, which will restrict his involvement as the team's training camp gets underway. he incident was announced by the team on Saturday, coinciding with the opening of camp.
An individual familiar with the incident, speaking anonymously to The Associated Press, revealed Shanahan suffered a concussion, a broken nose, several fractured ribs, and hand injuries.
The source requested anonymity as they were not authorised to discuss the matter publicly.
The 49ers organisation confirmed the injuries were "non-life-threatening" and expressed gratitude to emergency services who attended the scene last week.
With Shanahan sidelined, assistant head coach and offensive line coach Chris Foerster will oversee the team's initial practice on Sunday, supported by coordinators Klay Kubiak, Raheem Morris, and Brant Boyer.
Shanahan is entering his 10th season as 49ers coach and is one of the most highly regarded coaches in the game for his offensive acumen.
San Francisco has made two trips to the Super Bowl under his watch following the 2019 and 2023 seasons and made two additional appearances in the NFC title game in the 2021 and '22 seasons.
Shanahan has a 91-72 record in the regular season and playoffs for the 49ers, ranking third in franchise history in wins behind George Seifert (108) and Bill Walsh (102).
The team overcame significant injuries last season to finish 12-5 in the regular season and win a playoff game as Shanahan finished fifth in voting for the AP NFL Coach of the Year.

sources.news_title: 49ers’ Kyle Shanahan to be limited in camp after serious car crash
sources.text:
San Francisco 49ers head coach Kyle Shanahan broke his nose, three ribs and his hand, needed over 40 stitches to his face and sustained a severe concussion after he was involved in a car accident last week, ESPN reported Saturday.
Per the network, the accident occurred on July 14 after Shanahan collided with an SUV near his northern California home.
The other driver was not injured, per Palo Alto lieutenant Nicholas Martinez. Martinez added that drugs and alcohol were not involved.
The 49ers said Shanahan will participate in team activities on a limited basis at the start of training camp, with ESPN reporting doctors will not clear Shanahan for all activities until concussion symptoms clear.
The team said assistant head coach Chris Foerster along with team coordinators will handle the head-coaching responsibilities during this time.
49ers general manager John Lynch is scheduled to hold a news conference at 4 p.m. ET on Saturday.
The Niners are scheduled to hold their first practice of training camp Sunday morning and are set to open the season on Sept. 10 against the Los Angeles Rams in Melbourne, Australia.
Shanahan, 46, will begin his 10th season as head coach in San Francisco. He owns an 82-67 record in the regular season. He has a 9-5 postseason record, guiding the 49ers to a pair of Super Bowl appearances — losing to the Kansas City Chiefs both times (2020, 2024).

Proving the 49ers' recent inability to avoid injuries isn't limited to the players on the field, the team has announced that head coach Kyle Shanahan was involved in a serious car accident earlier this month that's left him with numerous non-life-threatening injuries that include a severe concussion.
A statement from the San Francisco 49ers issued on Saturday notes that Shanahan's car collided with an SUV near his California home on July 14. He was taken to a local hospital for treatment, where he was assessed as having suffered a broken nose, three broken ribs, a broken hand, and a severe concussion, per ESPN.
Shanahan also reportedly required over 40 stitches in his face. The other driver was apparently unharmed and authorities state they have ruled out the involvement of alcohol or drugs in the crash. At present, no citations have been issued in relation to the collision.
The incident occurs just as the San Francisco 49ers prepare to host their first practice for the upcoming season this weekend. According to the team statement, Shanahan has continued to recover at home but will participate in team activities "on a limited basis" once training camp begins.
Until Shanahan feels fully back up to speed, ESPN reports that assistant head coach Chris Foerster will tackle head-coaching duties for the 49ers. News of Shanahan's car collision comes after a season that saw star players Nick Bosa, Brock Purdy, Fred Warner, and George Kittle all miss notable time with serious injuries.
Assuming his recovery goes as planned, Shanahan will mark his tenth season as the 49ers' head coach when the team travels to Australia to face off against one of their NFC West rivals, the Los Angeles Rams, on Sept. 10.

sources.news_title: 49ers head coach Kyle Shanahan hurt in car crash, limited as training camp opens
sources.text:
San Francisco 49ers coach Kyle Shanahan suffered a concussion and other injuries in a car crash earlier this month that will limit his participation at the start of training camp, the team announced Saturday, when camp opened.
The two-car accident happened on July 14 in Palo Alto, leading to Shanahan being taken to the hospital. The other driver was not hospitalized. Palo Alto police Lt. Nicholas Martinez said there was no evidence that either driver was impaired and that both cooperated with police. No one was cited in the collision.
Niners general manager John Lynch said Shanahan sustained a concussion, along with a broken nose, broken ribs and an injured hand.
“Kyle is doing good,” Lynch said Saturday. “He’s got some bumps and bruises. He did suffer a concussion in the accident, has some lingering effects from that concussion.”
Lynch said Shanahan is going through the same type of protocol that players undergo after a concussion and that doctors would determine when he will be able to be back at full speed.
Lynch said Shanahan might be on the practice field when drills start on Sunday but won’t run practice or team meetings until he is recovered.
“He’s a tremendous head coach, but this is bigger than that,” Lynch said. “This is about his well-being. We’re going to take the time necessary. And I think we’re very equipped to do that.”
The Niners will conduct their first practice on Sunday with assistant head coach/offensive line coach Chris Foerster running the team, along with coordinators Klay Kubiak, Raheem Morris and Brant Boyer.
Foerster has been on the 49ers’ staff since 2019 and also worked under Shanahan in Washington as an offensive line coach when Shanahan was offensive coordinator.
Lynch didn’t give a timeline for Shanahan’s return but did say the team anticipates he will be back well before the season opener on Sept. 11 in Australia against the Los Angeles Rams.
Rams coach Sean McVay, who worked on the same staff as Shanahan in Washington from 2010-13, said he has talked to Shanahan since the crash and was thankful everyone involved was OK.
“I think any time that something like that happens, it shakes you up a little bit,” McVay said. “But most importantly, I’ve talked to him, my thoughts and prayers are with his family, and I know he’s got an incredible perspective on it all. Kyle is a stud. I have as much respect for him as anybody, and he’s a friend of mine and I love him, and I’m hoping that he’s going to have a great recovery.”
Shanahan is entering his 10th season as 49ers coach and is one of the most highly regarded coaches in the game for his offensive acumen. San Francisco has made two trips to the Super Bowl under his watch following the 2019 and 2023 seasons and made two additional appearances in the NFC title game in the 2021 and ’22 seasons.
Shanahan has a 91-72 record in the regular season and playoffs for the 49ers, ranking third in franchise history in wins behind George Seifert (108) and Bill Walsh (102).
The team overcame significant injuries last season to finish 12-5 in the regular season and win a playoff game as Shanahan finished fifth in voting for the AP NFL Coach of the Year.

49ers' Kyle Shanahan in car crash, suffers non-life-threatening injuries
San Francisco 49ers head coach Kyle Shanahan suffered "non-life-threatening injuries" in a recent car accident, according to a team statement.
The 49ers coach will be "limited" with the team as the 49ers enter training camp on July 25.
"San Francisco 49ers Head Coach Kyle Shanahan was involved in a car accident last week where he suffered non-life-threatening injuries. Coach Shanahan will participate in team activities on a limited basis at the start of training camp while he recovers," the team said in a statement.
"Coach Shanahan and the 49ers organization would like to sincerely thank all first responders involved for their efforts and care. Assistant Head Coach Chris Foerster, along with team coordinators, will handle head coach responsibilities during this period."
Dispatch received a call about a two-vehicle collision at the intersection of Alma Street and Hamilton Avenue near Stanford University on July 14 at 6:13 p.m., and Palo Alto Police Officers and Palo Alto Fire Department responded to the scene, Palo Alto Police Department Lt. Nicolas Martinez told USA TODAY Sports.
Two drivers were involved in the collision, and one was transported to a local hospital for treatment of injuries sustained during the crash. Martinez added that there was no impairment suspected and both drivers remained on scene and were cooperative with the police. No one was cited for the collision.
The 49ers' training camp is set for its first practice on July 26, ahead of their 2026 season opener on Thursday, Sept. 10 against the Los Angeles Rams in Melbourne, Australia, at the Melbourne Cricket Ground.
The 46-year-old Shanahan is in his 10th season with the team. He has a regular season record of 82-46 and a 9-5 mark in the postseason. He has twice taken San Francisco to the Super Bowl in 2019 and 2023, with both losses coming to the Kansas City Chiefs.

sources.news_title: 49ers’ Kyle Shanahan Suffered Multiple Injuries in Car Accident, Will Be Limited in Camp
sources.text:
49ers’ Kyle Shanahan Suffered Multiple Injuries in Car Accident, Will Be Limited in Camp
In this story:
49ers coach Kyle Shanahan will be limited during the start of training camp after sustaining multiple injuries during a car accident, per Adam Schefter and Nick Wagoner of ESPN.
Shanahan was involved in the car accident on July 14 when he collided with an SUV near his home in northern California, per ESPN. He suffered a broken nose, three broken ribs, a broken hand, a severe concussion, needed more than 40 stitches in his face and was taken to the hospital to be treated. He was released on that same day and has been recovering at home since. The other driver in the accident was not injured, and drugs and alcohol were not involved, according to local police.
“San Francisco 49ers Head Coach Kyle Shanahan was involved in a car accident last week where he suffered non-life-threatening injuries,” the 49ers announced in a statement. “Coach Shanahan will participate in team activities on a limited basis at the start of training camp while he recovers. Coach Shanahan and the 49ers organization would like to sincerely thank all first responders involved for their efforts and care. Assistant Head Coach Chris Foerster along with team coordinators will handle head coach responsibilities during this period.”
General manager John Lynch later told reporters on Saturday, “Kyle is doing good. He’s got some bumps and bruises. He did suffer a concussion in the accident, has some lingering effects from that concussion. We don’t have a protocol for staff members when it comes to concussions, but we do with players and it’s become very helpful. Kyle is basically going to be in the protocol. … We’re going to let the condition, the doctors dictate how he comes back, when he comes back.”
The 49ers report to training camp Saturday as they prepare for their 10th season under Shanahan. As Shanahan recovers from the accident, Foerster will take on the role of head coach in the interim. Shanahan will not be cleared for a full return until his concussion heals, and there is currently no timetable for his return. Foerster, who is also the team’s offensive line coach, has been with the franchise since 2019 and has over three decades worth of experience as an NFL assistant coach.
“We’re not going to blink,” Lynch said. “We feel we’re well-equipped for something like this. We understand what a tremendous leader we have in Kyle.”
San Francisco starts training camp earlier than the majority of teams this summer since they will be kicking off the season from Melbourne, Australia against the Rams. It is the furthest international game the NFL has held, and will take place on Sept. 10. Lynch noted that they expect Shanahan to be back before the trip to Australia.
The Rams also reported to training camp on Saturday. Coach Sean McVay, who is a friend of Shanahan, noted that he has spoken to him since the accident.
“Thank God he and the other person involved are okay,” McVay told reporters. “My thoughts and prayers are with him and his family. I know he’s got an incredible perspective on it all. Kyle’s a stud, I have as much respect for him as anybody. He’s a friend of mine. I love him and hope that he’s gonna have a great recovery.”
The 49ers are coming off a 12–5 season and a trip to the divisional round in 2025—one of Shanahan’s most impressive seasons as a play-caller—and are looking to build off that performance this year with many of their star players back healthy, too. Shanahan has been in the building and will be around during training camp, but for now, the 49ers are passing off head coaching duties as they look to prioritize their coach’s well-being and recovery.

The SF 49ers wrote a statement about Shanahan: “San Francisco 49ers head coach Kyle Shanahan was involved in a car accident last week where he suffered non-life-threatening injuries. More Details Revealed About Shanahan’s Car Accident
Kyle Shanahan is entering his 10th season as the head coach of the San Francisco 49ers. But his timeline to return to the team is to be determined after sustaining multiple injuries.

No one was cited for the collision.”

49ers assistant head coach and offensive line coach Chris Foerster is expected to assume some of Kyle Shanahan’s head coaching duties and help lead the team, according to Schefter.

San Francisco 49ers coach Kyle Shanahan injured in crash will see limited training camp participation
Kyle Shanahan, the San Francisco 49ers head coach, was injured in a crash and will have limited participation at the start of the team's training camp, the organization said Saturday.
Palo Alto police said the crash happened July 14, around 6:15 p.m., near Alma Street and Hamilton Avenue. It was a two-car crash, and one of the drivers was taken to the hospital.
Niners General Manager John Lynch said Shanahan had injuries that were not life-threatening but that he suffered a concussion and has lingering effects from the injury.
"We're kind of treating this … Kyle basically is going to be in the protocol," Lynch said. "We're going to let the condition, the doctors dictate how he comes back, when he comes back … It's kind of like what we do with our players: a phased-back approach. Number one for Kyle and the Shanahan family is getting him back right."
Shanahan's team responsibilities will be carried out by assistant head coach Chris Foerster and team coordinators, the 49ers said.
"Coach Shanahan will participate in team activities on a limited basis at the start of training camp while he recovers," the team said.
Neither driver is suspected of being impaired, and both were cooperative with investigators, police said. Officers did not cite anyone for the crash, and police said what led to the crash will not be released
"Coach Shanahan and the 49ers organization would like to sincerely thank all first responders involved for their efforts and care," the organization said.

sources.news_title: 49ers Kyle Shanahan suffers horrific injuries in car crash near California home
sources.text:
San Francisco 49ers coach Kyle Shanahan suffered horrific injuries — including a severe concussion — in a car crash near his Northern California home last week.
Shanahan’s vehicle collided with an SUV on July 14, leaving the coach with a broken nose, three broken ribs and a broken hand, according to ESPN. He also had to get 40 stitches in his face.
Shanahan was rushed to the hospital for treatment before being released later in the day, according to ESPN’s Adam Schefter. The other driver was uninjured.
Shanahan has been recovering at home and is believed to be progressing well, though doctors are not expected to clear him for full participation until his concussion symptoms subside. The team has not provided a timetable for his return.
Police said both drivers cooperated with investigators, and no citations were issued. Authorities have not disclosed the cause of the crash or said whether either driver was at fault.
“Consistent with our standard release of information procedures in such cases, we do not release information regarding the cause of the collision, or which party may have been at fault,” Palo Alto Lt. Nicholas Martinez said in a statement to ESPN.
Shanahan is expected to be limited as the team opens training camp on Sunday, according to the team.
“Coach Shanahan will participate in team activities on a limited basis at the start of training camp while he recovers,” the 49ers said in a statement. “Coach Shanahan and the 49ers organization would like to sincerely thank all first responders involved for their efforts and care.”
The team added that assistant head coach Chris Foerster and 49ers coordinators will step in to handle head coaching duties.
Shanahan only informed his fellow coaches of the wreck on Tuesday, ESPN reported.
He is still expected to coach the 49ers against the Los Angeles Rams in their Sept. 11 season opener overseas in Melbourne, Australia. The game will be the first regular-season NFL contest in Australia.
Rams head coach Sean McVay said he spoke to Shanahan after his car accident.
“Most importantly, thank God he and the other person involved is okay,” McVay told reporters.
Shanahan’s injuries will also not impact the team’s travel plans, 49ers GM John Lynch said during a press conference Saturday.
“I think the expectation is that before that he’ll be better,” he said. “We’re gonna do whatever it takes to have him right when he comes back, and that’s the right thing to do.”
The accident comes before a notable season for Shanahan. His 10th year with San Francisco will tie Bill Walsh for the longest coaching tenure in franchise history. Shanahan enters the season with 82 regular-season victories, third most in team history.
Ryan Anderson contributed to this report.

sources.news_title: 49ers coach Kyle Shanahan suffers significant injuries in car crash
sources.text:
A season after winning 13 games despite a deluge of injuries, the 49ers will begin preparation for their next campaign without the leader of that resilient effort — Kyle Shanahan.
The head coach, entering his 10th season with the 49ers, suffered a severe concussion in a July 14 car crash in Palo Alto. Shanahan — who reportedly needed more than 40 stitches in his face — also broke his nose, three ribs, and a hand. Palo Alto lieutenant Nicholas Martinez told ESPN neither driver involved in the crash (opens in new tab) was using drugs or alcohol.
Only general manager John Lynch was on hand for Saturday’s press conference to open training camp. This is unusual because Lynch and Shanahan had conducted this session together in each of the previous nine seasons.
“We’re not going to blink,” Lynch said. “We feel that we’re well-equipped for something like this.”
Lynch credited Shanahan, who’s led the 49ers to two Super Bowl appearances and five seasons with double-digit wins, for building the coaching infrastructure that can withstand an indefinite absence. (Lynch said Shanahan “has some lingering effects” from his concussion and will conduct duties that are cleared by doctors as he recovers.)
“One of the great things Kyle does aside from coaching this team is leading this organization,” Lynch said. “And I think he’s a tremendous developer of his staff. So we’re not going to miss a beat.”
Though the 49ers hope that Shanahan can fully heal and return well in advance of the team’s regular-season opener Sept. 11 in Melbourne, Australia, Lynch recognizes that the tricky nature of concussions can complicate matters. Shanahan will proceed through essentially the same concussion protocol that the 49ers apply to their players.
In the meantime, offensive line coach Chris Foerster will take over most of Shanahan’s executive duties while top coaches from various units — offensive coordinator Klay Kubiak, defensive coordinator Raheem Morris, and special teams coordinator Brant Boyer — will lead their groups.
Lynch pointed out that Foerster has 34 years of coaching experience, including 13 on staffs with Shanahan.
“He knows Kyle inside and out,” Lynch said. “What Kyle wants, what Kyle needs.”
Shanahan is best known for his offensive play-calling acumen. He’s been grooming Kubiak, who’s previously been entrusted with preseason play-calling duties, for that task.
“In training camp, Klay typically is doing that,” Lynch said. “Kyle has suggestions, but Klay does the [practice] script along with the staff, so nothing different there.”
This is the type of delegation that was introduced to the NFL by legendary 49ers coach Bill Walsh, who emphasized that effective leadership resulted in an operation that could continue humming even in the absence of its main architect. In a testament to the foundation Walsh laid, the 49ers went on the most dominant Super Bowl run of all time in 1989, the season after Walsh retired — outscoring their playoff opponents by a record 100 points.
An interesting side note: Walsh also suffered broken ribs during his coaching career. But unlike Shanahan, his injury happened on the field. A player collided with Walsh on the sideline during a brutal loss to the Phoenix Cardinals in 1988. It was a low point of a 49ers season that eventually featured a dramatic turnaround and a Super Bowl title.
3 readers have shared their thoughts on this story
Can these 2026 49ers, a veteran-laden squad featuring the league’s oldest offense and headlining players likely bound for the Hall of Fame on both sides of the ball, also reach that promised land?
Lynch, who spent some time with Fred Warner during an event at a local firehouse earlier this week, was encouraged by his star linebacker’s reaction to Shanahan’s injuries.
“Fred got back to Kyle right away,” Lynch said. “His message was, ‘We’ve got this, coach. Trust us.’
“So absolutely, the Trent Williams, the Kyle Juszczyks, the Christian McCaffreys, the Fred Warners, the Brock Purdys — we’ve got tremendous leadership. We’re not blinking. Our job is to be at our best.”
Extra points
• Perhaps the best news for the 49ers ahead of their first training camp practice on Sunday: Star edge rusher Nick Bosa is not on the physically unable to perform (PUP) list to begin training camp.
Bosa has been recovering from a torn ACL. He impressed Lynch by voluntarily rehabbing at the 49ers’ facility this offseason, forgoing his usual routine of returning home to Florida. Warner also trained at the facility, which encouraged younger players to follow suit.
“A lot of them are here because Fred Warner is here,” Lynch said. “It’s wonderful when your best players are your best leaders.”
Tight end George Kittle (torn Achilles), defensive end Mykel Williams (torn ACL), running back Isaac Guerendo (torn pectoral), and defensive tackle Alfred Collins (shoulder surgery) are all on PUP — but the 49ers are optimistic that all could return soon. Collins can even begin practicing by the end of this week.
The most high-profile recovery, of course, is Kittle’s.
“He’s doing everything possible to be ready for Week 1,” Lynch said. “We’re thrilled with his progress.”
• The 49ers waived rookie tight end Khalil Dinkins, who was on the non-football injury list. They signed tight end Tanner McLachlan to take his place. They also cut defensive tackle Evan Anderson, who joined the team as a undrafted free agent in 2024. That means there’s one open 90-man roster spot entering Sunday’s first practice.
• Lynch declined to delve into more specifics regarding receiver Brandon Aiyuk, who’s spent much of the past two months blasting the 49ers on social media.
“Brandon is on a left squad designation,” Lynch said. “As such, he’s not on our 90-man roster. And I personally, and we as an organization, are going to focus on the players that are here. I don’t have anything to add to that. We wish him well. We wish his family well.”
• The 49ers open the preseason with a home game on Thursday, August 13 against the Tennessee Titans. That regular-season opener in Australia against the Los Angeles Rams is on Thursday, September 10 Pacific Time (the game will kick off on Friday, September 11 at 10:35 a.m. in Melbourne).

sources.news_title: Banged-Up Coach: Kyle Shanahan To Open 49ers Camp On Limited Duty After Car Crash
sources.text:
San Francisco 49ers head coach Kyle Shanahan was involved in a car crash last week and came away with what the team is calling non-life-threatening injuries. He is still expected at training camp, but only in a limited capacity, while assistant coaches handle most of the on-field grind. The organization also publicly thanked first responders for their work.
In a short statement on 49ers.com, the club said Shanahan suffered non-life-threatening injuries and confirmed he will be limited at the start of camp while he recovers. The team did not offer any additional information about the crash itself or provide a timetable for he return to full duty.
According to CBS News Bay Area, there were no immediate details about where or how the accident happened, and Shanahan was not believed to be seriously hurt. CBS reported that assistant head coach Chris Foerster and the 49ers coordinators will take over head-coach duties while Shanahan is limited.
Who Will Run Camp While Shanahan Recovers
The 49ers said Assistant Head Coach Chris Foerster, along with the team's coordinators, will handle Shanahan's responsibilities during the opening stretch of camp. Foerster is listed as both assistant head coach and offensive-line coach and has been a long-serving member of the staff, which should help keep practices on schedule even with Shanahan stepping back. That setup shifts more of the day-to-day practice control to veteran position coaches while Shanahan operates in a scaled-back role.
Camp Timing And Immediate Impact
Veterans were scheduled to report to training camp today, with on-field sessions to follow. That timeline means the first practices could be run under Foerster's supervision, according to the San Francisco Chronicle. With Shanahan limited, early camp reps may be distributed a bit differently, and coordinators are likely to have more autonomy over installations and playcalling. The team has not released a specific timetable for his full return.
Why This Matters For The 49ers
San Francisco has spent recent offseasons harping on depth and recovery work after several years riddled with injuries, so any disruption to the coaching rhythm in camp is less than ideal. National coverage has highlighted that the 49ers have ranked near the top of the league in advanced injury metrics in recent seasons, which only raises the premium on clean, uninterrupted preparation. Even a short-term adjustment at the top can ripple through how practices are scripted and how workloads are managed.
For now, Shanahan is expected to remain with the team in a limited role while medical staff monitor his progress, and the 49ers said they will share updates as appropriate.

The 49ers are set to kick off the regular season on Sept. 10, when they face the Los Angeles Rams in the National Football League’s first ever game in Australia.
Lynch said Shanahan is “very eager” to be back on the field.
“He goes through a process like we all do to get ready for the season like we all do, like players do. … We see players go through a similair things and it’s no different when it’s our head coach.” Lynch said. “We’ll support him through that and I think it gives him great comfort to know, ‘We got your back, Kyle, until you’re ready.'”
This story will be updated as more information becomes available

sources.news_title: Niners' Kyle Shanahan will be limited in his coaching duties to start training camp following car crash
sources.text:
San Francisco 49ers head coach Kyle Shanahan was involved in a car crash on July 14 and will be limited in his coaching duties during training camp, the team announced on Saturday.
Assistant head coach Chris Foerster and team coordinators will handle head coaching responsibilities in the interim.
Shanahan suffered three broken ribs, a broken hand, broken nose, sustained a "severe" concussion and needed more than 40 stitches after colliding with an SUV near his Northern California home, ESPN reported.
"San Francisco 49ers Head Coach Kyle Shanahan was involved in a car accident last week where he suffered non-life-threatening injuries," the team said in a statement. "Coach Shanahan will participate in team activities on a limited basis at the start of training camp while he recovers. Coach Shanahan and the 49ers organization would like to sincerely thank all first responders involved for their efforts and care.
"Assistant Head Coach Chris Foerster along with team coordinators will handle head coach responsibilities during this period."
Shanahan, 46, was transported by paramedics to a hospital, where he spent "much of that day," per ESPN. The other driver involved in the collision was not injured. Drugs and alcohol were not involved, and citations were not issued for the crash.
No timetable has been given for Shanahan's full return, but he has not been cleared for all activities as a result of his concussion.
San Francisco reported for training camp Saturday as it begins its season in Australia against the Los Angeles Rams on Thursday, Sept. 10 -- the second game of the 2026 NFL season.
General manager John Lynch spoke to media Saturday and said the team is not "anticipating" that Shanahan will miss San Francisco's Week 1 opener.
"That's not what I've heard from the doctors, but just like we talk about with players, the timeline kind of takes care of itself," Lynch said. "So, he has to meet certain markers, but I think the expectation is that long before that he'll be better. But again, everybody responds to these things differently. We're going to do whatever it takes to have him right when he comes back."
Shanahan is entering his 10th season as head coach of the 49ers and sports an 82-67 record with five playoff appearances, three NFC West titles and two Super Bowl appearances.
Foerster, 64, has been part of Shanahan's staff since 2019. Elsewhere on the staff, new defensive coordinator Raheem Morris has six seasons of past experience as a head coach (Tampa Bay Buccaneers; Atlanta Falcons) and offensive coordinator Klay Kubiak is in his sixth year with the club and his second season as Shanahan's OC.

Shanahan suffered a concussion, broke his nose and several ribs, and injured his hands in the crash, a person familiar with the injuries told The Associated Press, speaking on condition of anonymity because the person wasn't authorized to discuss them.
The team described the injuries only as "non-life-threatening" and thanked first responders for their work at the scene of the crash last week.

sources.text:

The two-car accident happened on July 14 in Palo Alto, leading to Shanahan being taken to the hospital. The other driver was not hospitalized. Palo Alto police Lt. Nicholas Martinez said there was no evidence that either driver was impaired and that both cooperated with police. No one was cited in the collision.
Niners general manager John Lynch said Shanahan sustained a concussion, along with a broken nose, broken ribs and an injured hand.
“Kyle is doing good,” Lynch said Saturday. “He’s got some bumps and bruises. He did suffer a concussion in the accident, has some lingering effects from that concussion.”
Lynch said Shanahan is going through the same type of protocol that players undergo after a concussion and that doctors would determine when he will be able to be back at full speed.
Lynch said Shanahan might be on the practice field when drills start on Sunday but won't run practice or team meetings until he is recovered.
“He’s a tremendous head coach, but this is bigger than that,” Lynch said. “This is about his well-being. We’re going to take the time necessary. And I think we’re very equipped to do that.”
The Niners will conduct their first practice on Sunday with assistant head coach/offensive line coach Chris Foerster running the team, along with coordinators Klay Kubiak, Raheem Morris and Brant Boyer.

Rams coach Sean McVay, who worked on the same staff as Shanahan in Washington from 2010-13, said he has talked to Shanahan since the crash and was thankful everyone involved was OK.
“I think any time that something like that happens, it shakes you up a little bit,” McVay said. "But most importantly, I’ve talked to him, my thoughts and prayers are with his family, and I know he’s got an incredible perspective on it all. Kyle is a stud.
